rules:
Each player is dealt 5 cards face down. A betting round follows.

Each player may then discard up to the maximum discards allowed. The maximum is the Dealer's Choice.

The Dealer then deals the replacement cards (called the Draw). A final betting round follows.

displayName: 5-Card Draw — Jacks or Better to Open
rules:
5-Card Draw (Variant)

To open the first betting round, a player must have a pair of jacks or better.

If nobody can open, the cards are mucked and a new hand is dealt. The pot carries over to the new hand.

displayName: 5-Card Draw — Jacks or Better, Trips to Win
description: 5-Card Draw - Jacks or Better, Trips to Win
rules:
5-Card Draw (Variant)

To open the first betting round, a player must have a pair of jacks or better.

To win, a player must have 3 of a Kind or better.

If nobody can open or win, the cards are mucked and a new hand is dealt. The pot carries over to the new hand.

5-Card Stud

5 cards dealt per player: 1 down + 4 up.

2 cards dealt in first betting round (called 2nd Street). Player with the low card starts the betting with a forced-bet called the Bring-In.

1 card dealt for each of the next 3 betting rounds (3rd, 4th & 5th Streets). Player with the highest showing cards begins the betting in these rounds.

7-Card Stud

7 cards dealt per player: 2 down + 4 up + 1 down.

3 cards dealt in first betting round (called 3rd Street). Player with the low card starts the betting with a forced-bet called the Bring-In.

1 card dealt for each of the next 4 betting rounds (4th, 5th, 6th & 7th Streets). Player with the highest showing cards begins the betting in these rounds.

7-Card Stud Lowball (Variant)

LOWEST HAND WINS!

Rules for Low Hand is a Dealer Option.

On 3rd Street, highest card makes the Bring-In bet.

On 4th – 7th Street, lowest cards showing opens the betting.

Suit Ranking: Clubs < Diamonds < Hearts < Spades

7-Card Stud Split Pot (Variant)

High hand and Lowest QUALIFIED hand split the pot.

Low Hand Qualifications:
* Ace-To-Five ranking
* No Pairs
* No card higher than an 8
* Straights and flushes are not counted against the player

If there is no qualified low hand, then high hand takes the whole pot.

You may use different cards to play for both the High and Low hand.

7-Card Stud with Wildcards (Variant)

If and when a Queen is dealt face up, the next card dealt face up is wild. If another Queen is dealt face up, the next card dealt face up replaces the previous wildcard.

If the final card dealt face up is a Queen, then there are no wild cards.

7-Card Stud Wildcards (Variant)

Basics:
* 9s are always wild
* 3s are sometimes wild
* Players dealt a 4 face up may buy another card

Dealer Options To Watch For:
* Do 3s dealt face up require payment?
* Are all 3s wild or only face up or face down?
* Do 4s require payment to get an extra card

7-Card Stud Wildcards (Variant)

High / Low hands split the Pot.

Basics:
* 9s are always wild
* 3s are sometimes wild
* Players dealt a 4 face up may buy another card

Dealer Options To Watch For:
* Do 3s dealt face up require payment?
* Are all 3s wild or only face up or face down?
* Do 4s require payment to get an extra card
* What are the Low Hand Rules

7-Card Stud (Variant)

Winning the hand requires having BOTH the:
* Highest hand and
* Highest FACE DOWN spade

QUEEN OF SPADES –

If the Queen of Spades is dealt face up, the hand ends immediately.

If either the Queen of Spades comes up or no player meets the winning hand requirements, the cards are mucked and a new hand is dealt. The pot carries over to the new hand.

7-Card Stud Split Pot (Variant)

Pot is Split Between:
* Highest hand and
* Highest FACE DOWN spade
* Ace is highest card for spade down

Prior to showing hand, players must declare whether they are playing for the High hand, Highest Spade, or Both. If a player declares for "Both", he must win both in order to win anything.

If no spade is down, player winning the High hand wins the entire pot.

Any portion of pot not allocated carries over to the next game.

7-Card Stud Split Pot (Variant)

Pot is Split Between:
* Highest hand and
* Lowest FACE DOWN spade
* Deuce is the lowest card

Prior to showing hand, players must declare whether they are playing for the High hand, Lowest Spade, or Both. If a player declares for "Both", he must win both in order to win anything.

If no spade is down, player winning the High hand wins the entire pot.

Any portion of pot not allocated carries over to the next game.

Texas Hold'em

Opening Deal
Each player is dealt 2 cards face down.

The Flop
3 Community Cards are dealt to the center of the table.

The Turn
1 additional Community Card is added to the 3 already there.

The River
1 last Community Card is added, making 5 Community Cards.

A round of betting takes place after each of the 4 deals. After the River betting round, players make their best 5 card hand from their 2 down cards & the 5 community cards.

Texas Hold'em (Variant)

Same as Texas Hold'em with the following changes:
* 4 cards are dealt to each player in the opening deal
* To make their best hand, players must use exactly 2 of their down cards and 3 of the community cards

Omaha Split Pot (Variant)

High hand and Lowest QUALIFIED hand split the pot.

Low Hand Qualifications (Stud 8 rules):
* Ace-To-Five ranking
* No Pairs
* No card higher than an 8
* Straights and flushes are not counted against the player

If there is no qualified low hand, then high hand takes the whole pot.

You may use different cards to play for both the High and Low hand.
